effect_estimate.comment: No econometric or quantitative causal/associational estimate linking legal/institutional variables to outcomes is computed; quantitative figures are descriptive national/regional baseline trends from Plansab, SNIS, and DATASUS.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Doctrinal and institutional analysis concludes that Federal Law No. 14.026/2020 facilitates privatization of sanitation utilities and shifts decisions over plans and investments to contracted private companies, limiting civil society participation in municipal councils/forums and hindering universal water and sewage access for vulnerable peripheral populations. Descriptive secondary data (Plansab/SNIS, not linked via statistical estimation to the 2020 law) show national household water coverage rose from 90.0% (2010) to 93.0% (2015) and stagnated at 93.0% (2018), while sewage/septic coverage rose from 67.0% (2010) to 72.0% (2015) and 76.0% (2018), with 83.3% total (93.1% urban) public-network water coverage and 50.3% total (58.0% urban; 42.7% treated) sewage collection, and lowest coverage in the drought-vulnerable North and Northeast regions.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 3, Section 1; PDF pp. 8–9, Figures 2–4 and Table 1; PDF pp. 10–12, Sections 4–5
